title: Isolation of human fetal intestinal cells for single-cell RNA sequencing
protocol: Prepare tissue for digestion protocol or storage.
Receive intestinal tissue in 10 mL of transport medium on ice.
Proceed quickly with all dissection steps.
Place tissue on cutting board.
Examine fetal intestinal tissue under operating microscope.
Identify anatomical landmarks for orientation (stomach, appendix, Meckel’s diverticulum).
Isolate and separate 2 cm regions of tissue from the anatomical compartments of interest.
For low gestation tissue (<12 post-conceptual weeks), isolate and separate 1 cm regions of tissue.
Wash lumen with cold PBS to remove meconium.
Flush PBS into the lumen using a blunt needle and syringe or pipette tip.
Wash with 500 μL–1000 μL of PBS for at least three washes.
Dissect each sample further by opening the lumen and cutting it into small tissue fragments (e.g., 0.2 cm²).
Move all tissue fragments to tubes.
Wash each fragment with 10 mL of cold transport media.
Shake the tube and centrifuge.
(Optional) Fully aspirate all transport media from the tissue fragments.
Resuspend the tissue fragments in 500 μL of Cryostor CS10.
Place the tubes in a freezing container, such as CoolCell® or MrFrosty®.
Move the freezing container to a −80°C freezer.
Carry out all dissection steps on ice using reagents pre-cooled on ice.
Obtain supernatant enriched for epithelial crypts through EDTA chelation.
Centrifuge the tubes containing tissue fragments in transport media if processing fresh tissue.
Fully aspirate transport media and add 3 mL of ACK lysing buffer to the tube.
Shake the tube and incubate it at room temperature (18°C–22°C) for 5 min.
Add 10 mL of wash media and centrifuge.
Fully aspirate wash media.
Repeat previous steps then proceed to subsequent step.
Prepare a 50 mL tube containing 25 mL of thaw media using a serological pipette if processing frozen tissue.
Obtain samples from −80°C freezer and transport them on ice to the water bath.
Thaw samples in the water bath until only small ice crystals remain (estimated 2 min).
Immediately add thaw media to fill cryovial, mix three times, then transfer contents to the tube containing 25 mL of thaw media.
Agitate the tubes and centrifuge.
Aspirate thaw media and wash tissue with 10 mL of wash medium.
Proceed to subsequent step after washing.
Replace final wash media with 10 mL of pre-warmed chelation media.
Shake then incubate tubes in a water bath for 15 min.
Vortex or shake tube every 5 min for 5-10 s during each chelation step.
Allow tissue to settle after the last vortex.
Remove supernatant with FBS-coated pipette and transfer it to a new 15mL tube as crypt fraction 1.
Place the tube containing crypt fraction 1 on ice.
Leave approximately 500 μL of chelation media in the initial stages for tissue preservation if needed.
Add 5 mL of fresh chelation media to the tissue-containing tube.
Repeat steps 10–12.
Centrifuge the tube containing crypt fraction 1 while chelation is ongoing.
Resuspend small pellet in 2 mL cold transport medium in a new 15 mL tube and place it on ice.
After the second 15 min incubation, repeat steps 12 and 13 to obtain crypt fraction 2.
Pool crypt fraction 2 with crypt fraction 1 and place the resulting tube (now containing 4mL transport media) on ice.
Repeat chelation step by adding 5 mL of chelation medium and repeating steps 10–12 for crypt fraction 3.
During breaks between EDTA chelation steps, prepare stromal digestion enzymes.
Without re-adding chelation medium to the tissue, repeat steps 12 and 13 once again to obtain the third and last crypt fraction.
Pool all three fractions (6 mL) in a 15 mL tube and centrifuge it.
Fully aspirate remaining chelation media from the tissue.
Transfer the remaining tissue directly to stromal digestion in the incubator.
Resuspend all crypt fractions in 3 mL of warm TrypLE Express containing 50 μg/mL DNAse.
Incubate at 37°C for 35 min using continual agitation or rotation.
Move the remainder of the crypt-depleted tissue into the stromal digestion cocktail immediately after pipetting out the crypt fraction.
Prepare enzyme solution in a pre-warmed 24-well plate containing 700 μL of buffer L replacement.
Add 100 μL of Enzyme D, 62.4 μL of Enzyme P, 6 μL of Enzyme B, and 12 μL of Enzyme A to the enzyme solution.
Optimize enzyme volumes for small samples if necessary by using half volume of each enzyme in the cocktail.
Place the plate with crypt depleted fraction in the incubator for 45 min.
Bring out the plate every 15 min.
Use a blunt needle attached to a 2.5 mL syringe for mechanical dissociation.
Pull up and flush down the sample repeatedly using the needle and syringe.
Wash the needle in a 2 mL buffer L replacement well between uses.
Look at the sample under a microscope after 45 min.
Check for tissue disruption and single cell suspension.
Collect all stromal and epithelial suspensions.
Wash each tube with thaw media and centrifuge.
Place 70 μm cell strainers on top of 50 mL Falcons, one per condition.
Pre-wet the filter membrane using FBS.
Vigorously resuspend each pellet in 1 mL of thaw media.
Flush the suspension through the filter.
Add thaw media up to 10 mL and centrifuge.
Repeat the washing step.
Resuspend pellet in 1 mL of thaw media.
Flush through a 30 μm strainer pre-wetted with FBS.
Wash through with 3 mL of thaw media if using sample for downstream culturing/FACS, or with PBS + 0.04% BSA for scRNA-seq.
Centrifuge the suspension.
Resuspend cell pellet in 250 μL media or PBS + 0.04% BSA depending on downstream application.
Transfer exactly 250 μL to a new Eppendorf tube.
Take a sample of 10 μL for cell counting.
Mix it with 10 μL of 0.1% Trypan Blue.
Add the mixture to an Invitrogen Countess slide or view under hemocytometer for manual counting of cells and viability.
Proceed single cell suspension to further downstream use, such as loading for scRNA-seq on 10× Chromium platform, antibody staining for flow cytometry, or scRNA-seq multiplexing.
